sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: CC Switch is a desktop app for managing AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode. It lets you switch API providers in one click and manage MCP servers, skills and prompts in one place.
sixtySeconds.problem: Each AI coding tool keeps its own config in JSON, TOML, YAML or .env files, so changing providers or adding an MCP server means editing several files by hand. CC Switch handles that from one app and only replaces the connection details.
whoFor: Developers who use several AI coding CLIs
People who switch between API providers or accounts
Users who want MCP servers and skills synced across tools
Anyone who wants to track token usage and quotas
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you juggle several coding agents or providers and want a GUI instead of editing config files. If you use one tool with one account, you probably don't need it.
requirements: Windows 10+, macOS 12+, or Linux x86_64/ARM64 with glibc 2.35+ and WebKitGTK 4.1

overview: CC Switch is a native desktop app built with Tauri 2 that manages twelve tools, including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. It has more than 90 provider presets, including AWS Bedrock and NVIDIA NIM, and switching changes only the endpoint, key and model.

Besides direct connections, a Routing mode forwards requests through your machine to convert API formats and fail over automatically, and Aggregation mode combines models for Claude Code and Codex. MCP servers and skills are added once and synced to the tools you choose.

It also reads each tool's session logs into a readable view, shows token usage, spending and remaining quotas, and can install or upgrade the coding tools themselves. On first launch it imports your existing configuration as a provider named default.

features.title: One-click provider switching
features.body: Pick a preset, enter your key and switch.

features.title: Twelve tools in one app
features.body: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes and more.

features.title: Shared MCP and skills
features.body: Add MCP servers and skills once, then sync them to chosen tools.

features.title: Routing and failover
features.body: Convert API formats locally and fail over between providers.

features.title: Readable sessions
features.body: See what each turn did, which files changed and which step failed.

features.title: Usage and quotas
features.body: Track tokens, spending and remaining quota per provider.

strengths: Keeps your own plugins, hooks and comments when switching
limitations: Some tools need a restart after switching
Older enterprise Linux (RHEL/Rocky/Alma 8–9) isn't supported yet
Third-party relay providers in its presets are separate services; check their terms yourself

useCases.title: Switch Claude Code providers
useCases.body: Move between an official login and an API provider in one click.

useCases.title: Sync an MCP server
useCases.body: Add it once and enable it for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI.

useCases.title: Review a session
useCases.body: Open the reading view to see what an agent changed.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from CC Switch's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Download the installer
steps.body: Get CC-Switch-v{version}-Windows.msi (or the portable .zip, or the arm64 .msi on Windows on ARM) from the GitHub Releases page and run it.

steps.title: Other distros
steps.body: Download the .deb, .rpm or .AppImage for your architecture from the Releases page.

firstRun.title: Open CC Switch
firstRun.body: It imports your existing Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok Build config as a provider named default.

firstRun.title: Add a provider
firstRun.body: Pick a tool in the sidebar, click + and choose a preset.

tutorial.title: Switch Claude Code to a different API provider
tutorial.useCase: Add a provider preset and switch Claude Code to it.
setup: An API key for the provider you want

steps.title: Select Claude Code in the sidebar
Click + (Add Provider)
steps.body: Choose a preset or create a custom configuration and enter your key.

steps.title: Click Enable on the provider
steps.body: Claude Code needs no restart. Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok Build need a terminal restart.

steps.title: Go back to the official login anytime
steps.body: Switch to the built-in Claude Official provider, restart the tool and log in.

tutorial.expected: Claude Code uses the new provider, and your own plugins, hooks and MCP settings are unchanged.

troubleshooting.solution: Restart your terminal or the CLI for Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok Build, and restart Claude Desktop itself.
Switch to the built-in official provider, restart the tool and follow its login flow.
It needs glibc 2.35+ and WebKitGTK 4.1, for example Ubuntu 22.04+ or Debian 12+.

bestFor: People using several AI coding CLIs
